acceptance_basis: Full-length ceiling compounded from P-BLOCK-PUR over P-N-BLOCKS (EQ-PURITY). An assumption, not a specification.
notes: The first anchor point, as data: this is the control that sets the purity ceiling, and it sits OUTSIDE the facility. No downstream separation can raise it, because block-internal n-1 differs from the product by one nucleotide in the middle of a strand. No in-facility instrument enforces it - the enforcement is an incoming specification and a supplier certificate. The measured basis is 89-96 percent for 4-5 nt modified blocks (SRC-WO2020227618), which are NOT our 5'-phosphate blocks (Q-011). A route that omits capping makes this worse by converting coupling failures into deletions rather than truncations (R-018).

acceptance_basis: P-LIG-CONV per ligation, compounded over the assembly (EQ-LIG). Assumption.
notes: Conversion is what decides how much whole-block impurity is introduced, and unlike the block floor it IS adjustable in-facility. The cited figure is per-ligation, not a step mass yield (P-YLD-LIG), and it comes from a 5 mL packed column at 600 uM - a different scale and a different enzyme format from a kg-scale batch (Q-010, Q-050).

cpp: ATP concentration in the ligation reaction
acceptance_basis: P-LIG-ATP as charged into the ligation buffer. Assumption, and a CONTESTED one - though the conflict is a coupling with a known reconciling mechanism, not an empty feasible region (Q-040).
notes: This row is where the control strategy contradicts itself and says so. REWRITTEN 2026-09-25 because the contradiction was overstated. The 'at least 4 mM ATP' sentence is verbatim in SRC-WO2025262452 and appears twice, but it states THE PROBLEM THAT DOCUMENT'S INVENTION SOLVES, not an operating condition: the same document teaches 'less than about 4 mM ATP ... optionally ... 0.5 mM or less', says its ATP regeneration system 'overcomes the requirement for high concentrations of ATP', and claims complete ligation with 'sub-stoichiometric quantities of ATP or AMP'. The suppression side is softer too - SRC-PBCV1-2014 reports little inhibition at 1 mM ATP for most sequences, not a hard ceiling at 100 uM. So the earlier reading, that the feasible window is empty at every demonstrated titre, is NOT supported and is not written. What remains is a genuine two-way coupling with a mechanism that reconciles it - in-situ regeneration from AMP and polyphosphate, exemplified in the very document cited for the high bound - and a second coupling nobody had registered: ATP chelates magnesium roughly one-for-one, so the ATP charge draws down free Mg2+ in a 10 mM MgCl2 buffer and propagates into the hardest clearance gap in the register (IMP-DIVALENT, R-014). Both are in couplings.csv. The optimum still moves with the enzyme form (Q-050) and the dead end cannot be filtered out afterwards (R-010). The acceptance basis is a placeholder with a live coupling attached, not a setpoint (Q-040).

Both cited ligation examples ran at the same temperature, in two different regimes with two different enzymes - agreement, but not a demonstrated optimum for ours (Q-050). A higher setpoint would also move the reaction closer to the duplex melting band (P-DS-TM, Q-030, R-003), so this parameter is bounded from above by a limit nobody has measured for our sequence.

acceptance_basis: The reaction is held to a conversion endpoint, not to a clock; P-LIG-TIME is the band that has been demonstrated and is an expectation rather than a limit. The endpoint TEST exists and is demonstrated on this buffer, but its limit of quantitation, its precision and the rule for declaring conversion stationary are all unregistered (Q-067).
notes: The instrument named here is the conversion IPC, not a timer, and that is the point: a hold time is an outcome of the reaction reaching its endpoint. STRENGTHENED 2026-09-25 after checking whether this control was executable at all. It is: the demonstrated method runs in 12.5 min on our exact buffer (SRC-ALMAC-2023 SI Table S3) and the reaction moves about 0.70 points per hour near the endpoint, so the 0.35-0.70 points lost to a 30-60 min turnaround sit against 1.40 points of remaining travel (SRC-USPTO-10640812 Table 22). What is genuinely wrong is narrower and is now registered: this row names no method, no LOQ, no precision and no stopping rule (Q-067). A rule of the form 'change of no more than X points between successive samples at one hour or more spacing' is the SHAPE required; no value for X is written here, because none is published and inventing one would be a specification nobody measured. Note also that the demonstrated IPC is DENATURING - its oven runs at 80 C, above P-DS-TM - so it answers the denaturing dimension only (Q-044). And nothing terminates the reaction when the sample is drawn (R-022, C-014). The band brackets two different enzymes at two different temperatures, and whether a batch hold is even the right regime depends on the enzyme form (Q-050, Q-010).

BLANK acceptance basis, deliberately. Stating a loading here would silently choose an enzyme form, and that choice is open (Q-050). This row exists because it SIZES the clearance problem two rows below: the one cited loading is a cell-free-extract loading, which puts a whole proteome plus endotoxin through purification rather than one enzyme (R-017). The loading is set by what is charged, so no instrument measures it directly - the two named instruments measure its consequence in the clarified pool.

NO CONTROL IS DEFINED, and this row says so rather than implying one. The proposed mitigation is to suppress AppN at the reaction by lowering ATP, but that pulls directly against the ATP a multi-ligation assembly needs (Q-040) - so the mitigation in R-010 is a direction, not a control. The instrument named can SEE the species; nothing in this register prevents it. The dead end differs from the product by about 329 Da, so filtration cannot remove it downstream.

cpp: Powder glass transition at the achieved residual moisture
notes: The BINDING thermal limit on drying and storage, and the second anchor point as data. BLANK acceptance basis: the glass transition is a function of OUR matrix and OUR achieved moisture (EQ-TG, Gordon-Taylor), and neither is fixed - the excipient ratio is open (Q-021) and so is where the excipient enters (Q-038). The band that exists was measured on spray-dried trehalose siRNA polyplex formulations at their own moisture, not ours (Q-039). The pair of parameters travels together because a glass transition quoted without the moisture it was measured at is detached from its condition.

acceptance_basis: Outlet gas temperature held below the duplex melting temperature, as a conservative proxy for the particle (P-DRY-T-OUT below P-DS-TM). The LOOSER of the two thermal limits.
notes: The relation is the acceptance basis; the bound is not known. The melting band that exists is for a 21-mer with three modified positions in 100 mM NaCl, not our fully modified duplex, and the authors' per-position increment must not be extrapolated across all 21 positions (Q-030). The outlet setpoint itself is an assumption (Q-046). Tier 2 stated this limit as the duplex control; it is the looser one - the glass transition above binds first (Q-039).

cpp: Final diafiltration matrix and excipient ratio
acceptance_basis: Final diafiltration exchanges into a spray-dryable matrix at P-EXCIPIENT-RATIO. Assumption.
notes: The third leg of the duplex-integrity argument: the matrix sets the glass transition the row above is measured against (EQ-TG). Non-volatile buffer salts concentrate through evaporation into the powder unless the final exchange removes them (R-005). The ratio is a placeholder (Q-021) and where the excipient enters swings the evaporation duty severalfold (Q-038), so this row is a formulation choice standing in for a formulation decision nobody has made.

cpp: Ligase clearance - soluble branch, denature then depth filtration
cqa: Residual enzyme protein in the drug substance
notes: ONE OF TWO BRANCHES, NEITHER CHOSEN. Blank acceptance: no log-reduction, ppm or immunoassay figure for ligase clearance exists in the public record for either branch (Q-032). This branch is not free - the cited denature condition is a heat kill well above any plausible duplex melting band, which trades an enzyme-clearance gap for a product-integrity risk (R-021, P-DS-TM, Q-030) - and the cited route follows the heat kill with an ion column rather than filtration alone (R-002). It also needs a heated vessel or exchanger that DOES NOT EXIST in the equipment register: U02-CF is single-use depth media and cannot denature anything. That missing unit is registered against Q-050 rather than invented here.

cpp: Ligase clearance - immobilised branch, retention on the carrier
cqa: Residual enzyme protein in the drug substance
notes: THE OTHER BRANCH, EQUALLY UNCHOSEN. Blank acceptance for the same reason: no log-reduction, ppm or immunoassay figure for ligase clearance exists publicly for either branch (Q-032), and it is now also clear that no LIMIT exists to clear to (Q-060) and no ASSAY exists that works in this matrix (Q-061). The one demonstrated immobilised route uses IMAC-type non-covalent immobilisation, so retention on the carrier is the claim that would have to be demonstrated rather than assumed. CROSS-REFERENCE ADDED 2026-09-25: this branch now carries R-021 too. It previously read as the branch that escapes the thermal hold, and that is refuted - SRC-CN119265174 Example 12 runs the IMMOBILISED arm through 85 C/15 min on the same terms as the soluble arm, and Example 12 is the only example in that patent that measures product purity or endotoxin at all. Immobilisation may also make the enzyme HARDER to kill: in SRC-NEB-WO2023173098 Example 3, titled verbatim 'IMMOBILIZED T4 DNA LIGASE DISPLAYS STABILITY INCLUDING THERMOSTABILITY', soluble ligase showed 'no or residual ligase activity after treatment at 45 C for 30 min' while the benzylguanine-agarose form retained activity at 55 and 65 C - and magnetic beads gave no protection at all, so the effect is carrier-dependent. A kill validated on a soluble enzyme therefore cannot be assumed to inactivate the immobilised form. TWO DUTIES THIS BRANCH CARRIES THAT THE REGISTER DID NOT NAME: the carrier itself is a process-related impurity under ICH Q6B s6.2.1(c), which lists 'carriers' and 'ligands' and 'other leachables' by name; and the demonstrated carrier is a nickel-iminodiacetic-acid agarose run in a buffer containing 1 mM DTT, which is the highest-leaching common chelator in a reducing buffer, with nickel, ligand and desorbed enzyme all unmeasured (Q-032, Q-060). If retention fails, enzyme removal reverts to chromatography and the filtration-led thesis breaks (R-002).

cpp: Retentate concentration at the UF/DF endpoint
acceptance_basis: Endpoint judged on a WITHDRAWN sample by variable-pathlength slope spectroscopy (I-024), against the registered target P-CONC-UF. The loop is OPEN: there is no in-line reading to close it on this stream, because the pathlength an A260 = 1 reading needs at P-CONC-UF falls below the published in-line floor P-VPE-PATHLENGTH-MIN.
notes: THE ROW THIS SLICE EXISTS TO MAKE EXPRESSIBLE, and the row whose first version got the reason wrong. What is true: fixed-pathlength in-line UV saturates on a 21-mer at process concentration, and at P-CONC-UF the required pathlength (a few um, computed in gen/controls.py from P-EPS-260) sits below the published in-line floor P-VPE-PATHLENGTH-MIN, so the reading must come off a withdrawn sample. What was WRONG and is now corrected: this row previously said variable-pathlength slope spectroscopy IS at-line and that no in-line instrument exists. It is not a property of the technique - FlowVPE publishes 5 um to 8 mm and is used in-line on UF/DF in the peer-reviewed literature (SRC-ROLINGER-2023, SRC-BHANGALE-2022), and FlowVPX catalogues a 260 nm GMP light source (SRC-REPLIGEN-FLOWVPX). So this is a PROJECT constraint on THIS stream, not an impossibility, and the control type says at_line_only rather than not_measurable. Residual gaps that would have to close before it could ever be an in-line loop are in Q-051, including that FlowVPX never publishes a minimum pathlength and that no oligonucleotide A260 data exists for either instrument. Watch the failure mode: variable-pathlength cells saturate near their own floor and UNDERESTIMATE concentration.

NO CONTROL IS DEFINED, and this row exists to say so rather than to imply one. The reaction has a start and a conversion endpoint and no stop: 'quench', 'inactivat', 'EDTA', 'chelat' and 'proteinase' return zero hits across every non-sources register in this repository. param_ref is blank because this is a gap row, and the parameter that WOULD be named - P-LIG-INACT-T - deliberately carries a band with no point value, because the step may not exist at all. THE EVIDENCE CONTRADICTS ITSELF INSIDE ONE DOCUMENT, which is why this is a gap and not a choice: SRC-CN119265174 heat-kills an immobilised enzyme at 80 C for 5 min in Example 7 and both an immobilised and a soluble arm at 85 C for 15 min in Example 12, yet in Examples 3, 5, 6 and 8 it takes the immobilised enzyme out by centrifugation at 3000 rpm for 2 min with no thermal step whatever - and Example 8 is immobilised AND batch AND unheated, which refutes both the soluble-versus-immobilised and the batch-versus-flow readings of when a hold is needed. Every documented process inactivation runs at 80-95 C, above the whole measured duplex melting band, so choosing one is choosing R-021. The mitigation the sources point at and nobody has demonstrated here is to chelate first: EDTA stops the reaction, strips the cofactor so the enzyme cannot resume on cooling, removes the hydrolysis catalyst, and turns free Mg2+ into a net-negative complex that diafilters where the free cation does not (R-014, IMP-DIVALENT). That is an inference from two retrieved facts, not a demonstrated condition, so it is written here as a direction and not as an acceptance basis. No instrument is named because a gap has nothing enforcing it. See Q-059, R-022, R-021, C-005.
